environment.deployment: Docker Desktop; API, MySQL 8, Redis 7 and Kafka on one host; Dify containers stopped during timed rounds

scope: authenticated end-to-end seckill admission; 10000 distinct in-memory local benchmark JWT users per measured round

method.warmup: each fresh API process received one excluded 10000-request warm-up and drained Reservation pending before measured rounds
method.baseline: distributed Redis sliding-window rate limit + one sales.tick Kafka event per accepted order
method.optimized: bounded local-fast sliding-window protection + 50ms per-SKU sales.tick semantic coalescing
method.common: async recoverable Reservation, activity Caffeine cache, Redis Lua inventory, 128 Tomcat threads, 20 Hikari connections, 3 Kafka consumers

semanticCoalescing.safetyBoundary: sales.tick only wakes rule evaluation to read current Redis stock; durable order.created and Reservation remain per order

excludedRuns.reason: optimized process inherited baseline Reservation backlog and hit the explicit 10000 pending recovery gate
excludedRuns.use: recovery-gate evidence only; excluded from capacity medians

excludedRuns.reason: an earlier 100-request warm-up made the first comparison asymmetric; replaced by an excluded 10000-request warm-up for each fresh process

limitations: Load generator and all services shared one physical host; this is a local engineering A/B, not a production SLO.
Three 10000-request measured rounds reduce but do not eliminate host scheduling and JVM variance.
local-fast mode is intended for one API instance; multi-instance deployments should retain distributed mode or fuse admission into the Reservation Lua script.
The combination was measured as a unit; the report does not attribute the 17.59% gain separately to either optimization.
